solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: a pun is a joke made by playing on words
to shed is to drop, as a tree drops its leaves

explanation.surface: Someone got a telling-off because their joke fell flat and they let it fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chastised and being punished both mean being made to suffer for a wrongdoing; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Cue for politician to withhold love

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: withhold means keep back, so the letter for love is kept out of the word to

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A signal for an MP to hold back their affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withhold love' takes O out of TO, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is a word given to an actor who has forgotten a line, which is what a cue does on stage.

indicators.note: off means bad or gone wrong, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The men give their figure a rubdown at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a numeral or figure, such as 7 or 42.

clue.text: Darned small woolly animal with odd tail

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
a ewe is a female sheep, a woolly animal

indicators.note: tail is the end of the word that follows, its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone mended a little sheep that has a strange tail, or a knitted toy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Darning is mending a hole by stitching, so darned means sewed in that sense.

clue.text: Working Danes have rights and jobs

indicators.note: have means hold, so the shuffled letters hold the two Rs
working means in motion or being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, so two Rs are rights

explanation.surface: Employed Danes are entitled to proper work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' makes EANDS, and 'have' holds the two Rs just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Errands are short trips to carry out small tasks, so they are jobs or chores.

clue.text: Saw the innards of fleshy supine Swedes

indicators.note: innards are the insides, so take the central letters of each of the three six-letter words that follow

explanation.surface: A gruesome scene: someone glimpsed the guts of plump Swedes lying face up.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word has six letters, so 'the innards of' gives the central pair from each: ES, PI and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is a literary verb for catching sight of something, so its past tense means saw.

clue.text: Saint gagged and put on the rack

parts.note: to gag is to retch, to heave as if about to vomit

explanation.surface: A martyr was silenced and then tortured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gagged' reads as silenced in the martyr story, but here it means heaved.
explanation.definitionFit: The rack was a torture frame that pulled the body; anyone put on it was stretched by it.

clue.text: I would love the French to attempt reverence

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
la is French for the, feminine form
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone longs to have a go at French-style worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is the worship of idols, an extreme form of devoted reverence.

clue.text: Ask nerds to dissipate the gloom

indicators.note: dissipate means scatter, so these letters are scattered into another order

explanation.surface: An appeal to the geeks to lift everyone's low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is deep shade with little light, so it is a synonym for the lack of light.

clue.text: Showing exclamation of surprise, I swear!

definitions.note: a promise that one is telling the truth, like 'honestly!'

parts.note: a play or film that is on is showing
'my word!' is a cry of astonishment

explanation.surface: Someone displays their astonishment and then vows they are telling the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a pledge on one's honour that something is true, an oath like 'honestly!'

clue.text: Protection from weapon belonging to us

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in 'firearm' or 'bear arms'
our is the word meaning belonging to us

explanation.surface: We own a weapon that keeps us safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is the metal covering worn or fitted to shield a body or vehicle from attack, so it is protection.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to skip a few of the toiletries when packing.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to exclude it or fail to include it, which is to leave it out.

clue.text: Also known as rubbish dump, nosey!

definitions.note: the phrase stands for the alternative name it introduces, a noun sense

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash or wreck, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A nosy neighbour is told off about the rubbish tip, under a false name perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Also known as' is the 'aka' that introduces an alias, so it stands for the false name itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is an assumed name, the kind that follows 'aka' when someone is also known by another name.

indicators.note: back says the word art is to be read backwards

parts.note: Art's here is 'Art is', the art going backwards

explanation.surface: Art has returned to the timetable at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art's back' is read as 'Art is back', the 's serving only as the verb, with 'back' turning the word round; 'school' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or drill them, which is what training means as a verb.

definitions.meaning: writes quickly, as a letter or note is scribbled down
enclosures for animals, as in a farmyard

explanation.surface: Someone rushes away and then their engine cuts out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means writes something down; as a plural noun it means small fenced enclosures for livestock.

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A teenager of sixteen is muddled about church life.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence is the state of being alive, so it means life.

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not says the letters of the word fine are to be removed from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Frugality goes out of the window when it comes to buying fancy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes F, I, N, E from THRIFTINESS, leaving THRITSS, which 'fancy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tees with short sleeves and no collar are everyday garments, so the plural is a type of clothes.

parts.note: even so means still, nevertheless

explanation.surface: A complaint that the service remains useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' reads as customer care in the surface; it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service in the Anglican church.

indicators.note: build means put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: An order to be the first to construct an oil platform.
explanation.definitionFit: The original of something is the first one, from which copies are made.

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the criminal is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: a conversion is a change from one form or belief to another
a con is a convict, a criminal serving time

explanation.surface: A crook decides to go straight and leave their criminal type behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A version is a particular form or variety of something, so it means a sort or kind.

clue.text: Bugger all nitrogen, oxygen and neon

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
Ne is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: A chemist's sigh: nothing left but three gases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugger all' is coarse British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing at all is not one, and the slang phrase means exactly that: zero, nothing.

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at the other way, so the hidden run is turned round
part of says a run of letters is taken from inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A grumble that one step in a process was nasty when it was looked at again.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude behaviour is impolite and offensive, so the word fits unpleasant as a description of manners.

clue.text: Get over always eating crushed ice

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the other letters go inside
over means turned over, so the word for always is turned round

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'for ever'

indicators.note: crushed means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recovers by always chewing crushed ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives REVE and 'crushed' gives CEI; 'eating' puts the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive something is to be given it, so it means to get.

indicators.note: including says one piece holds the other

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A price cut on French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving is a reduction in what you pay, just as a discount is.

clue.text: In this way initially you prevent fever

indicators.note: In placed before the way-word signals that the other letters go into it

parts.note: thus means in this way

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the two words after it

explanation.surface: Advice on how to ward off a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes Y and P, which go inside THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhus is an infectious disease marked by high fever, so it is a fever by name.

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near
T stands for a junction shaped like the letter, a T-junction

explanation.surface: A road sign: the motorway exit numbered 8 is close by.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a motorway junction number but points to the answer at 8 down, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-referenced answer at 8 down means the absence of light, which is what the hours after sunset bring.

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Stagehands move the backdrops only when they have to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something necessary cannot be done without, so it is needed or required.

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: cedes means surrenders or gives up

explanation.surface: Someone loudly surrenders their nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts are the seeds of certain plants, inside a hard shell, so they are a kind of seed.

clue.text: Having this hurts neither Italians nor Greeks to begin with

parts.note: ow is the cry someone makes when something hurts

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Someone claims that possessing something causes pain to neither Italians nor Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this hurts' is a cryptic way of asking for the exclamation itself: the cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something is possessing it, which is what having means in the sense of holding as property.

parts.note: the right is one side, as with left or right of a road
a dish is slang for an attractive person, a looker

explanation.surface: Someone's companion turns out to be a handsome figure on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' flags that right is an example of a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A smaller plate served alongside a main course, such as salad or fries, goes with the meal as an accompaniment.

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: olden means belonging to an old time, as antique does

explanation.surface: A dealer praises a superb Georgian antique, perhaps a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgian here means from the reign of Britain's King Georges (1714–1830), a period prized by antique dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden can describe something that shines like gold, so it is brilliant in the sense of bright and gleaming.

indicators.note: contains says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a jam or mess is a difficult fix to be in
sage is a kitchen herb

explanation.surface: A jar of preserve has herbs in it, perhaps with tasting notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages are communications passed on in writing, and short written messages are notes.
